text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Polish Airlines LOT want to start operating a regular Warsaw-Toronto connection. LOT has applied for permission to the Canadian government and is awaiting a decision.
- The French-British GEC Alsthom concern has acquired a controlling stake in the Chorzow-based Konstal rolling stock maker but has not revealed the value of the purchase.
- The Centertel analogue mobile phone company and the Plus GSM digital phone firm have agreed on connections between the two networks' subscribers.
- The German-Polish venture Gerolsteiner Poland last month opened a new soft drinks plant which cost DEM 16 million to build in Reniszew, Czestochowa province.

- The Polish Chamber of Commerce (KIG) environment committee has opposed the creation of 20 natural preserves in the middle Vistula-river region as this could affect river transport and weaken flood control in the area.

- In the third round of Polish-Israeli talks on a free trade agreement, Poland demanded that Israel give up customs duties on cables while Israel wanted Poland to cut duties on computer systems, Poland's foreign trade ministry said.
- The Bankowe Towarzystwo Leasingowe leasing association's net profit in the first nine months of 1996 amounted to 14 million zlotys.
NOWA EUROPA

- The Pioneer Polski Dom Maklerski brokerage house will start a new "blind portfolio" service for shareholders such as stock market journalists, Securities Commission members and employees, politicians, and all those who should not operate independently on the stock market for ethical reasons.
- Lecturers of the Danish people's university will train a group of longterm unemployed people in the Nidzica region of northeastern Poland, where there is structural unemployment.
- Former president Lech Walesa will lobby for an official invitation to a Taiwanese government delegation to visit Poland, despite protests by Beijing.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Poland's honey production this year decreased by almost 50 percent compared with last year, due to the long, cold winter which killed 30 percent of all bees, Skierniewice-based horticultural institute researcher Andrzej Pidek said.

- The Indukta electrical engineering firm has bought the Ostrzeszow-based EMA-ELFA electrical equipment plant in Western Poland. Indukta guaranteed it would preserve the present employment level in the factory.
- Daewoo-FSO repaid the car factory's past debts to the state treasury this August, company spokesperson Krystyna Danilczyk said.
- Despite Poland's good economic results, 80 percent of Poles think their financial situation is as bad as it was three years ago or worse, an OBOP polling institute survey showed.
ZYCIE
- Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) bank will not be privatised by the end of April 1997, despite previous plans, as the finance ministry first wants to privatise Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy.
- Poland's agricultural machinery sales grew by 6 percent this year and mineral fertiliser consumption grew by 4.3 kg per hectare, the agricultural economy institute said.
PARKIET
- CS First Boston in its October report recommended buying the listed Krosno and selling Irena glassmakers' shares.
- The listed Elektromontaz-Export electrical engineering firm will distribute mobile phones and subscriber cards to Era GSM digital mobile phones' subscribers.
- The listed Novita carpet maker's sales revenues in the first 10 months of 1996 amounted to 55 million zlotys.
